nodes.d: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s (1:1), is a poem of dialogue between a bride, her beloved and the daughters of Jerusalem, praising mutual love from first longing to its strength (8:6-7).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the speakers in the Song of Solomon and the theme of the poem?
ev: Name the speakers in the Song and the main settings (gardens, vineyards, the city, the wilderness).

nodes.t: Longing and praise: the first meeting
nodes.d: The bride longs for her beloved and speaks of him as a bundle of myrrh; he praises her as a lily among thorns, and she says she is sick of love, charging the daughters of Jerusalem not to awaken love before it pleases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} identify who is speaking in Song of Solomon 1-2:7 and what they say about each other?
ev: Find the speakers in 1:2-4 and 2:1-7 and list the images used for love.

nodes.t: Arise, my love: the voice of the beloved in spring
nodes.d: The bride hears her beloved coming over the mountains and he calls her to arise and come away because the winter is past and flowers appear; she asks for the little foxes to be caught, and says my beloved is mine and I am his.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the invitation in Song of Solomon 2:10-13 and the bride’s answer in 2:16?
ev: Read 2:10-13 and list the signs of spring.
Read 2:16 and say what the bride says of the two of them.

nodes.t: Seeking him whom my soul loves
nodes.d: By night the bride seeks her beloved in the city, is found by the watchmen, and then finds him and holds him until she brings him to her mother’s house; she again charges the daughters of Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the search in Song of Solomon 3:1-4?

nodes.t: Solomon’s bed and the daughters of Zion
nodes.d: A procession is described coming out of the wilderness with smoke of myrrh and frankincense around the bed of Solomon with sixty valiant men, and the daughters of Zion are called to behold king Solomon with his crown on his wedding day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the scene of 3:6-11 and name who is being looked at?
ev: Read 3:6-11 and list what is carried and who accompanies it.

nodes.d: The beloved praises his bride at length, calls her my spouse, his garden enclosed and a spring shut up; she invites him to come into his garden, and he says he has come into his garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the garden images in Song of Solomon 4:12-5:1?
ev: Read 4:12-5:1 and list the images of the garden and what the bride and groom say.

nodes.t: I opened to my beloved, but he was gone
nodes.d: The bride hears her beloved knocking at night, hesitates, and opens to find him gone; the watchmen strike her, and she asks the daughters of Jerusalem to tell him she is sick of love; they ask what is her beloved, and she describes him, saying he is hers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the events of Song of Solomon 5:2-8 and what the bride says in 6:3?

nodes.d: The beloved praises his bride as beautiful as Tirzah and comely as Jerusalem, says there are many queens and concubines but she alone is his dove, and in chapter 7 admires her form and desires her; she says I am my beloved’s and his desire is toward me.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the bride says of herself and her beloved in Song of Solomon 7:10?
ev: Find 6:8-10 and 7:10 and say what is said of the bride.

nodes.t: Come, let us go forth into the field
nodes.d: The bride invites her beloved to go forth into the field and lodge in the villages and give him her love there; she wishes he were as her brother, and charges the daughters of Jerusalem once more not to awaken love before it pleases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the bride invites her beloved to do in Song of Solomon 7:10-13?
ev: Read 7:10-8:4 and list what the bride offers.

nodes.d: The bride asks to be set as a seal upon his heart, saying love is strong as death and many waters cannot quench it; the closing verses speak of a little sister, Solomon’s vineyard, and the bride calling her beloved to come quickly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Song of Solomon 8:6-7 and explain what it says about love?
ev: Read 8:6-7 and list the images used for the strength of love.
